samples.summary: design-sandbox compiles real frontend source but its `define` block was not updated with the new `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` global, so sandbox scenes will silently diverge from the app build
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:405-419` adds a new build-time constant `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, read by `packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:supportsClientKey()`. `packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:185-197` renders *real frontend source* (its own comment at line 187-192: "Mirrors `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts`. Scene source IS real app source") and defines `process.env`, `__APP_VERSION__` and `import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` — but not the new global. There is a scene pointed straight at the changed page: `packages/design-sandbox/scenes.config.json:214-233` (`settings-personal`, file `packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx`), and the canvas scenes at 235-354 render the editors that host `SyncStatusChip`. It does not crash — `yorkie-capabilities.ts:75` guards with `typeof` and falls back to `'0.0.0'` — but it means `supportsClientKey()` is hard-wired `false` in the sandbox, so the new `Offline` section (`settings/page.tsx`, gated on `offlineAvailable`) and the chip's offer branch can never be rendered or design-reviewed there, and the two builds will disagree the moment `@yorkie-js/react` is bumped past `MinClientKeyVersion`. Fix belongs in the sandbox config (add the same define), not in the new code.

samples.summary: The new purge in `deleteDocuments` (and its test) is justified by a partial-`deleted` response the backend endpoint never produces — it is all-or-nothing
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:212-215` and `documents.test.ts:152-159` state "The route is manager-gated per id, so a partial answer is ordinary." The other side of that contract, `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:400-437`, is all-or-nothing: it collects `denied` ids and throws `ForbiddenException` for the whole batch (lines 419-423) if *any* id is not manageable, and on success returns `{ deleted: body.ids }` (line 437) — the full input list. So `result.deleted` can only ever be all of `ids` or the call throws. The code still behaves correctly (`result.deleted ?? []`), but the comment and the test case "drops the local copy of only what the server says it deleted" encode a server behaviour that does not exist, which will mislead the next person reasoning about whether a local copy can survive a delete.

samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime`'s session housekeeping (`GET /documents` + an IndexedDB open/scan) runs on every authenticated mount with no capability or preference gate, including on the current pin where the feature can never store anything
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:64-175` runs its effect on `[userId]` alone: it constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore`, calls `retryPendingOfflineErase()`, `store.collectStale()`, then `fetchDocuments()` followed by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments(...)`. None of that is gated on `supportsClientKey()` or `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`. It is mounted from `packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:35`, which wraps *every* authenticated route (`packages/frontend/src/App.tsx:139-187` — settings, analytics, datasources, invite accept, all six editors). On the pinned `@yorkie-js/react` 0.7.22 (`packages/frontend/package.json:66`, below `MinClientKeyVersion` 0.7.23) `supportsClientKey()` is false, so nothing can ever have been written — yet every signed-in page load now issues an extra full cross-workspace document listing (`packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195`, unpaginated over every workspace the user belongs to) and opens IndexedDB. That is a new, permanent cost on an unrelated backend endpoint and on browsers that refuse storage, for work that is provably a no-op on this build.
